requirements_summary: Dedicated pool with deterministic baseline throughput and documented burst capacity. Tight latency SLOs for chat (95p <= 150ms token latency), reranking tail latency 99p <= 300ms under baseline load. Reserved GPU planning: initial commitment 8x A100-class GPUs with 25% headroom for autoscale bursts. Hard uptime target 99.95% (monthly). Support and maintenance explicit in contract.
sla_terms_draft: Uptime target: 99.95% monthly for Dedicated service (excl. scheduled maintenance)
Credit schedule (proposal v2): <99.95%-99.90% => 10% monthly credit; <99.90%-99.50% => 30% credit; <99.50% => 60% credit or termination right after 2 incidents
Latency SLOs: 95th percentile token latency <= 150ms, 99th percentile <= 350ms for chat endpoints at committed throughput
Throughput guarantee: baseline 5k tokens/sec sustained across the dedicated pool; burst up to 15k tokens/sec for up to 10 minutes with 30m cool-down
Reserved GPU plan: commit 8 GPUs initially (A100 equivalent), capacity review at months 3 and 6 to adjust pool sizing
Maintenance windows: monthly 02:00-04:00 PT rolling with 48h notice; emergency maintenance allowed with 3h notice for critical security patches
Data residency: customer data to remain in us-west region; backups encrypted with customer KMS key
maintenance_policy: Planned: monthly 2-hour rolling window (02:00-04:00 PT) with 48h notice. Emergency: customers notified within 3 hours; maintenance minimized and documented. Redwood to provide post-maintenance report and metrics for any impact.
support_response_sla: Severity 1 (service down / critical impact): initial response <= 30 minutes, engineer engaged <= 1 hour, dedicated war room until resolution
Severity 2 (major degradation): initial response <= 2 hours, target remediation 8 hours
Severity 3 (minor impact): initial response <= 1 business day
Support hours: 24/7 for Sev1/2, business hours for Sev3. Premium enterprise 15-minute paging available as add-on
poc_plan: Week 0: NDA/PO executed and VPC peering set up
Week 1-2: Baseline perf tests — 95/99p latency and throughput at committed GPU count
Week 3: Synthetic burst tests to validate autoscale and eviction/fallback behavior
Week 4-8: Canary in production with shadow traffic; monitor QoQ regressions and cost metrics
Acceptance: 30-day canary with no SLO breaches and pass of security checklist
commercial_terms: Initial reserved commit: 8 GPUs, 12-month term; 3-yr pricing option requested by procurement
Burst buffer pricing: pay-as-you-go above committed throughput; optional reserved burst pool for discounted rate
Termination / early-exit: pro-rated refund subject to 90-day notice; triggers on repeated SLA failures under credit thresholds
